subproblems.title: The divergence of a C¹ field compactly supported in the open unit cube integrates to zero over the cube
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). If g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is C¹, has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ Q₁, then ∫_{Q₁} div g = 0, where div g(y) := trace Dg(y) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof ("for every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0"), with the integration along lines written as an integration by parts on ℝⁿ. In Simon this is the fact, implicit in displays (29)–(30) of the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1876), that subtracting the constant multiple β[[F]] does not change the boundary inside F̊.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let g be C¹ with compact support K := tsupport g ⊆ Q₁.

1. Regularity. Dg : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is continuous (g is C¹), and Dg(x) = 0 for x ∉ K: such an x has the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ ∖ K on which g ≡ 0, so g is locally constant at x (Mathlib support_fderiv_subset: support (fderiv ℝ g) ⊆ tsupport g). Hence for every fixed h ∈ ℝⁿ the map x ↦ Dg(x)h is continuous with support in the compact set K, so it is integrable on ℝⁿ; likewise g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. The map A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), hence continuous, so x ↦ div g(x) is continuous, vanishes outside K and is integrable on ℝⁿ.

2. Directional derivatives integrate to zero. Fix h ∈ ℝⁿ. Apply integration by parts on ℝⁿ (Mathlib integral_smul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_smul_of_integrable, Lebesgue measure on Euclid n) to the scalar function f ≡ 1 and the vector function g in the direction h. Its hypotheses hold: x ↦ Df(x)h • g(x) = 0 is integrable, x ↦ f(x) • Dg(x)h = Dg(x)h is integrable by 1, x ↦ f(x) • g(x) = g(x) is integrable by 1, f is differentiable everywhere and g is differentiable everywhere (C¹). It gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Df(x)h • g(x) dx = −∫ 0 = 0. Import note: this lemma is in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts, which is not in the import closure of the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean; add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts` to Submission.lean (accepted nodes of this run add Mathlib imports in the same way). Alternative route inside the closure, needed only for h = e_i in step 3: identify Euclid n with Fin n → ℝ (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and split off coordinate i (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, x = Fin.insertNth i t x'); by Fubini ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∂_i g_k = ∫_{x'} (∫_ℝ (d/dt) g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') dt) dx', and for each x' the inner integral vanishes by MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable (t ↦ g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') is C¹ with compact support, so it and its derivative are integrable on ℝ).

3. Trace in the standard basis. Let e_1, …, e_n be the standard orthonormal basis of Euclid n. For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, trace T = Σ_i ⟨e_i, T e_i⟩ (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Hence div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ for every x. Since v ↦ ⟨e_i, v⟩ is a continuous linear functional and x ↦ Dg(x)e_i is integrable, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ dx = ⟨e_i, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)e_i dx⟩ = ⟨e_i, 0⟩ = 0 by step 2. Summing over i: ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

4. Restriction to Q₁. By step 1, div g vanishes outside K ⊆ Q₁, so the integrand of ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g vanishes off Q₁ and ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). By step 3 this is 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dg is continuous and vanishes off tsupport g ⊆ Q₁, so Dg(·)h, g and div g are integrable on ℝⁿ.
Integration by parts against the constant function 1 gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = 0 for every direction h.
div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg e_i⟩, so ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, ∫ Dg e_i⟩ = 0.
div g vanishes off Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (gradient bound for the mollified u_σ by duality with the fields φ̌_σ ∗ g, which are supported in Q₁) together with the convergence u_σ → u·1_{Q₁} in L¹ used in its steps 3 and 5. The duality is applied directly to a bounded measurable field g (the smoothing is carried by φ̌_σ), so the smooth cut-offs g_k and the monotone-convergence step of the parent proof are not needed. In Simon this is the mollification fact Ch. 2, 2.5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 543–545) as used in the proof of Ch. 2, 2.7 (lines 651–661).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Fix u, V with u integrable on Q₁ and hyp(u, V), and fix δ > 0.

0. V ≥ 0: the map g ≡ 0 is C^∞, has compact support, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ Q₁ and |0| ≤ 1; D0 = 0 and trace 0 = 0, so hyp gives 0 = ∫_{Q₁} u · 0 ≤ V.

1. Mollifier. Fix φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ, C^∞, φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, with support in the open unit ball (e.g. the normalized Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = 1/2, rOut = 1). For σ > 0 put φ_σ(z) := σ^{−n} φ(z/σ): φ_σ is C^∞, φ_σ ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, support φ_σ ⊆ B_σ(0) := {|z| < σ}, and A_σ := sup_z ‖Dφ_σ(z)‖ < ∞ (Dφ_σ is continuous with compact support). (One may equally take the normalized ContDiffBump with rIn = σ/2, rOut = σ.) Let ū := 1_{Q₁} u, which is integrable on ℝⁿ, and u_σ(x) := ∫ ū(y) φ_σ(x − y) dy (the convolution ū ⋆ φ_σ).
Import note: the convolution lemmas HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right/left and HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right/left used below are already available under `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`, but ContDiffBump.normed (Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed), ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le (Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Convolution), Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense) and, if used, gradient (Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic; InnerProductSpace.toDual, already available, suffices) are not. Add these imports to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean (accepted nodes of this run already import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense); with them the instances HasContDiffBump (Euclid n), IsAddHaarMeasure, Measure.Regular and IsNegInvariant for volume on Euclid n all resolve, and the frozen child types still elaborate unchanged.

2. Smoothness and derivative of u_σ. Since φ_σ is C^∞ with compact support and ū is locally integrable, u_σ is C^∞ and Du_σ(x)h = ∫ ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)h dy for all x, h (differentiation under the integral sign; Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right and HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right with L = ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ). Also |u_σ(x)| ≤ (sup φ_σ) ∫|ū|, so u_σ is bounded.

3. Gradient bound: for 0 < σ < δ, ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Du_σ‖ ≤ V.
 (a) Let ∇u_σ(x) ∈ ℝⁿ be the gradient (Du_σ(x)h = ⟨∇u_σ(x), h⟩, |∇u_σ(x)| = ‖Du_σ(x)‖; it is continuous). Define g(x) := ∇u_σ(x)/|∇u_σ(x)| if x ∈ Q_δ and ∇u_σ(x) ≠ 0, and g(x) := 0 otherwise. Then g is Borel measurable, |g| ≤ 1, g = 0 off Q_δ (so g is integrable on ℝⁿ), and Du_σ(x)(g(x)) = 1_{Q_δ}(x) ‖Du_σ(x)‖ for every x.
 (b) Define g̃(y) := ∫ φ_σ(x − y) g(x) dx. With φ̌_σ(z) := φ_σ(−z) (C^∞, compact support) this is the convolution g̃(y) = ∫ φ̌_σ(y − x) g(x) dx = (φ̌_σ ⋆ g)(y). (i) g̃ is C^∞ and Dg̃(y)h = ∫ (Dφ̌_σ(y − x)h) g(x) dx = −∫ (Dφ_σ(x − y)h) g(x) dx (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left and HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left; chain rule Dφ̌_σ(z) = −Dφ_σ(−z)). Taking the trace in the standard orthonormal basis (trace T = Σ_j ⟨e_j, T e_j⟩): div g̃(y) = −∫ Σ_j (Dφ_σ(x − y)e_j) g_j(x) dx = −∫ Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dx. (ii) |g̃(y)| ≤ ∫ φ_σ(x − y)|g(x)| dx ≤ ∫ φ_σ = 1. (iii) If g̃(y) ≠ 0 there is x ∈ Q_δ with φ_σ(x − y) ≠ 0, i.e. |x − y| < σ; then |x_i − y_i| < σ, so δ − σ < y_i < 1 − δ + σ for all i. Hence tsupport g̃ ⊆ P := {y : δ − σ ≤ y_i ≤ 1 − δ + σ for all i}, a closed bounded (hence compact) set with P ⊆ Q₁ because 0 < δ − σ and 1 − δ + σ < 1. So g̃ has compact support and tsupport g̃ ⊆ Q₁. The same holds for −g̃, and D(−g̃) = −Dg̃, div(−g̃) = −div g̃.
 (c) Applying hyp(u, V) to −g̃: −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃ ≤ V.
 (d) Identity. The function (x, y) ↦ ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ and bounded in absolute value by A_σ |ū(y)| 1_{Q_δ}(x), which is integrable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ (its integral is A_σ ‖ū‖₁ vol(Q_δ) < ∞). By step 2 and Fubini, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Du_σ(x)(g(x)) dx = ∫_x ∫_y ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dy dx = ∫_y ū(y) (∫_x Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dx) dy = ∫_y ū(y)(−div g̃(y)) dy = −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃, by (b)(i) and ū = 1_{Q₁}u.
 (e) By (a), (d), (c): ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Du_σ‖ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} Du_σ(x)(g(x)) dx = −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃ ≤ V. (If δ ≥ 1/2 then Q_δ = ∅, g = g̃ = 0, and the bound reads 0 ≤ V, which is step 0.)

4. L¹ convergence: ∫_{ℝⁿ} |u_σ − ū| → 0 as σ → 0⁺ (continuity of translation in L¹).
 (a) L¹ contraction. For f integrable on ℝⁿ and f_σ := f ⋆ φ_σ, Tonelli and ∫φ_σ = 1 give ∫|f_σ| ≤ ∫∫ |f(y)| φ_σ(x − y) dy dx = ∫|f|. By linearity of convolution, ∫|u_σ − h_σ| ≤ ∫|ū − h| for every integrable h, where h_σ := h ⋆ φ_σ.
 (b) Continuous compactly supported h. Let h be continuous with compact support S. Then h is uniformly continuous; put ω(σ) := sup{|h(x − z) − h(x)| : x ∈ ℝⁿ, |z| ≤ σ}, so ω(σ) → 0 as σ → 0. Since h_σ(x) − h(x) = ∫ φ_σ(z)(h(x − z) − h(x)) dz, |h_σ(x) − h(x)| ≤ ω(σ) for all x (Mathlib ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le gives exactly this bound for normed bumps). For σ ≤ 1, h_σ − h vanishes outside the compact set S₁ := {x : dist(x, S) ≤ 1}. Hence ∫|h_σ − h| ≤ vol(S₁) ω(σ) → 0.
 (c) Given ε > 0 choose h continuous with compact support and ∫|ū − h| < ε (density; Mathlib Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). Then ∫|u_σ − ū| ≤ ∫|u_σ − h_σ| + ∫|h_σ − h| + ∫|h − ū| ≤ 2ε + ∫|h_σ − h|, so limsup_{σ→0⁺} ∫|u_σ − ū| ≤ 2ε. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, ∫|u_σ − ū| → 0.

5. Conclusion. Put σ_k := δ/(k + 2) (so 0 < σ_k < δ and σ_k → 0) and v_k := u_{σ_k}. By step 2 each v_k is C^∞, in particular C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1). By step 3, ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V for every k. Since Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ and ū = u on Q₁, and v_k is bounded while u is integrable on Q_δ (so v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ), 0 ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| = ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − ū| ≤ ∫_{ℝⁿ}|u_{σ_k} − ū| → 0 by step 4. Hence ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0 as k → ∞. ∎

subproblems.title: Poincaré inequality on the cube Q_δ for C¹ functions, double-integral form
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, δ ≥ 0 and Q_δ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). For every C¹ function v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ∫_{x ∈ Q_δ} ∫_{y ∈ Q_δ} |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ √n ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖, with 2ⁿ√n = 2^{m+1} √(m + 1) and ‖Dv(x)‖ the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (v : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (δ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 v → 0 ≤ δ → ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |v x - v y| ≤ 2 ^ (m + 1) * Real.sqrt (m + 1) * ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ‖fderiv ℝ v x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (smooth Poincaré inequality on a cube of side s ≤ 1), stopped at its intermediate double-integral bound ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s · 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫|∇v| and specialized to Q' = Q_δ. In Simon this is the "usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions" invoked in the proof of Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 651–658).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let v be C¹ and δ ≥ 0. Write Q := Q_δ, s := 1 − 2δ ≤ 1 and F(x) := ‖Dv(x)‖ ≥ 0, a continuous function.

0. Trivial case and finiteness. If s ≤ 0 then Q = ∅ and both sides are 0. Assume 0 < s ≤ 1. Then vol(Q) = sⁿ, Q is convex, and |x − y| ≤ √n s for x, y ∈ Q (each |x_i − y_i| < s). v and F are continuous, hence bounded on the compact closure of Q; so all integrands below are bounded measurable functions on sets of finite measure, every integral is finite, the iterated Bochner integral on the left equals the iterated Lebesgue integral of the nonnegative function |v(x) − v(y)|, and Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative continuous integrands below.

1. Segment estimate. For x, y ∈ Q, γ(t) := v((1 − t)x + t y) is C¹ on [0, 1] with γ'(t) = Dv((1 − t)x + t y)(y − x). By the fundamental theorem of calculus, |v(y) − v(x)| = |∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt| ≤ ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + t y) |y − x| dt ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + t y) dt.

2. Integrating over Q × Q and using Tonelli for (x, y, t) ↦ F((1 − t)x + t y) ≥ 0 on Q × Q × [0, 1]: ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 J(t) dt, where J(t) := ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dy dx.

3. Bound for t ∈ [1/2, 1]. Fix x ∈ Q. The map y ↦ (1 − t)x + t y is a translate of the dilation by t, whose Jacobian determinant is tⁿ; by the change-of-variables formula for dilations and translations of Lebesgue measure (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos or MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul, together with translation invariance MeasureTheory.integral_add_left_eq_self; all integrands are bounded measurable on bounded sets, so the Bochner versions apply), ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dy = t^{−n} ∫_{(1 − t)x + tQ} F(z) dz. By convexity, (1 − t)x + tQ ⊆ Q, and F ≥ 0, so this is ≤ t^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F. Integrating over x ∈ Q (measure sⁿ): J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F.

4. Bound for t ∈ [0, 1/2). By Tonelli, J(t) = ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dx dy. Fix y ∈ Q; the map x ↦ (1 − t)x + t y has Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n} and maps Q into Q (convexity); as in step 3, ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dx ≤ (1 − t)^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F, and integrating over y ∈ Q gives J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F.

5. Conclusion. By steps 2–4, ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s · 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F = 2ⁿ √n s^{n+1} ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≤ 2ⁿ √n ∫_Q ‖Dv‖, because 0 < s ≤ 1 and ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≥ 0. With n = m + 1 this is 2^{m+1} √(m + 1) ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: If δ ≥ 1/2 the cube is empty; otherwise s = 1 − 2δ ∈ (0, 1], vol(Q_δ) = sⁿ and |x − y| ≤ √n s on Q_δ.
FTC on segments: |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 ‖Dv((1 − t)x + ty)‖ dt.
Tonelli and the affine change of variables (Jacobian tⁿ or (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, image in Q_δ by convexity) give J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖.
Hence ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ 2ⁿ √n s^{n+1} ∫‖Dv‖ ≤ 2ⁿ √n ∫‖Dv‖.

subproblems.title: Poincaré inequality on the unit cube for functions of variation at most V
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure), div g := trace Dg. If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, then there is c ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} |u − c| ≤ 2^{n+1} √n V = 2^{m+2} √(m + 1) V.

Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Poincaré inequality for u via the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0), run with the double-integral form of step 2 so that no means over Q_δ are needed; the final c is the mean u_{Q₁} = ∫_{Q₁} u, as in the parent proof. In Simon this is the BV Poincaré inequality Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 629–661) as used for the first line of display (32) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1883–1892).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Sibling results used. smooth_approx (cmcdt_cbm_smooth_approx): for u integrable on Q₁ with hyp(u, V) and δ > 0 there are C¹ functions v_k with ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0. smooth_poincare (cmcdt_cbm_smooth_poincare): for C¹ v and δ ≥ 0, ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀ ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ with K₀ := 2ⁿ√n = 2^{m+1}√(m+1).

Fix u integrable on Q₁ and V with hyp(u, V).

0. V ≥ 0: apply hyp to g ≡ 0 (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ∅ ⊆ Q₁, |0| ≤ 1; D0 = 0, trace 0 = 0): 0 = ∫_{Q₁} u·0 ≤ V.

1. Finiteness. Since u is integrable on Q₁ and vol(Q₁) = 1 < ∞, the function (x, y) ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |u(x)| + |u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁ (product of the restricted measures; it is a.e.-strongly measurable as a composition of the a.e.-strongly measurable functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y)). For every x and every δ ≥ 0 the function y ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (u is integrable there and constants are integrable on sets of finite measure), so h_δ(x) := ∫_{Q_δ} |u(x) − u(y)| dy is finite, 0 ≤ h_δ(x) ≤ |u(x)| + ∫_{Q₁}|u|, and by Fubini x ↦ h_δ(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable on Q₁; hence h_δ is integrable on Q₁. Put D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ} h_δ(x) dx = ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ} |u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.

2. D(δ) ≤ K₀ V for every δ ∈ (0, 1/2). Fix such δ and take v_k from smooth_approx (δ > 0). Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ, so v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ and ε_k := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0 is the L¹(Q_δ) distance. By smooth_poincare (δ ≥ 0), D_k := ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ K₀V. For all x, y: |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| + |u(x) − v_k(x)| + |v_k(y) − u(y)|. Integrating in y over Q_δ (all three terms are integrable in y) and then in x over Q_δ, and using vol(Q_δ) ≤ 1: D(δ) ≤ D_k + vol(Q_δ) ε_k + vol(Q_δ) ε_k ≤ K₀V + 2ε_k. Letting k → ∞ gives D(δ) ≤ K₀V.

3. D(0) ≤ K₀ V. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 3) for j ∈ ℕ; then δ_j ∈ (0, 1/2), δ_j ↓ 0, and every x ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. For x ∈ Q₁, 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| → 1_{Q₁}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| for every y ∈ Q₁, dominated by |u(x) − u(y)|, which is integrable in y over Q₁ for every x (step 1); so by dominated convergence h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. Moreover 0 ≤ 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x) h_{δ_j}(x) ≤ h_0(x) with h_0 integrable on Q₁, and 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x) h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. By dominated convergence D(δ_j) = ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_{δ_j}} h_{δ_j} → ∫_{Q₁} h_0 = D(0). Since D(δ_j) ≤ K₀V for all j by step 2, D(0) ≤ K₀V.

4. Choice of c. Let c := ∫_{Q₁} u. Since vol(Q₁) = 1, for a.e. x ∈ Q₁: u(x) − c = ∫_{Q₁}(u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − c| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy = h_0(x). Integrating over Q₁: ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| ≤ D(0) ≤ K₀V = 2ⁿ√n V ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V, the last step because V ≥ 0 (step 0). With n = m + 1, 2^{n+1}√n = 2^{m+2}√(m + 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0 from g ≡ 0; |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁, so D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ}∫_{Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| is finite.
For δ ∈ (0, 1/2): smooth_approx gives v_k, smooth_poincare gives D_k ≤ 2ⁿ√n V, and D(δ) ≤ D_k + 2∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u|; letting k → ∞, D(δ) ≤ 2ⁿ√n V.
δ_j = 1/(j+3) ↓ 0 and dominated convergence give D(0) = ∫_{Q₁}∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| ≤ 2ⁿ√n V.
With c = ∫_{Q₁}u (vol Q₁ = 1), ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| ≤ D(0) ≤ 2ⁿ√n V ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.

subproblems.title: Integer median on the unit cube: it minimizes the L¹ deviation and is bounded by twice the L¹ norm
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ takes only integer values and is integrable on Q₁, then there is β ∈ ℤ with ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ and |β| ≤ 2 ∫_{Q₁}|u|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ β : ℤ, (∀ c : ℝ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - c|) ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let u be integer-valued and integrable on Q₁. Write μ for Lebesgue measure restricted to Q₁; μ(ℝⁿ) = vol(Q₁) = 1, and for a set A we write μ{P} for μ{y : P(y)}.

0. Measurability reduction. u is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ, so there is a Borel function u' with u = u' μ-a.e. Put ũ(y) := round(u'(y)) (nearest integer, a Borel map ℝ → ℤ ⊆ ℝ). Since u is integer-valued, round(u(y)) = u(y), so ũ = u μ-a.e.; ũ is Borel and integer-valued. All quantities in the statement (∫_{Q₁}|u − β|, ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|, ∫_{Q₁}|u|) are unchanged when u is replaced by ũ, so we may and do assume u Borel measurable. (Alternatively, work with the μ-null-measurable sets {u ≤ c}.) All functions |u − c| are μ-integrable because μ is finite.

1. Distribution function. F(c) := μ{u ≤ c} is nondecreasing in c. As k → ∞ through ℕ, {u ≤ k} increases to ℝⁿ (u is real-valued), so F(k) → μ(ℝⁿ) = 1 by continuity from below; and {u ≤ −k} decreases to ∅, so F(−k) → 0 by continuity from above (μ is finite). Hence S := {k ∈ ℤ : F(k) ≥ 1/2} is nonempty (contains large k) and bounded below (F(−k) < 1/2 for large k, and F is monotone). Let β := min S (Mathlib Int.exists_least_of_bdd).

2. Median properties. F(β) = μ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 and F(β − 1) < 1/2. Since u is integer-valued, {u > β − 1} = {u ≥ β}, so μ{u ≥ β} = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2. Consequently μ{u > β} = 1 − μ{u ≤ β} ≤ 1/2 and μ{u < β} = 1 − μ{u ≥ β} < 1/2.

3. Minimality: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ.
 Case c ≥ β. Pointwise, on {u ≤ β} we have u ≤ β ≤ c, so |u − c| − |u − β| = (c − u) − (β − u) = c − β; on {u > β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −|c − β| = −(c − β) by the triangle inequality. Integrating over Q₁: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (c − β)(μ{u ≤ β} − μ{u > β}) ≥ (c − β)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.
 Case c < β. On {u ≥ β}, |u − c| − |u − β| = (u − c) − (u − β) = β − c; on {u < β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −(β − c). Integrating: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (β − c)(μ{u ≥ β} − μ{u < β}) ≥ (β − c)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.

4. Size of β. If β > 0: on {u ≥ β}, |u| ≥ u ≥ β, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β μ{u ≥ β} ≥ β/2. If β < 0: on {u ≤ β}, |u| ≥ −u ≥ −β = |β|, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β| μ{u ≤ β} ≥ |β|/2. If β = 0 the claim is trivial since ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ 0. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|. ∎

β := least integer k with vol(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ k}) ≥ 1/2 exists by continuity of the distribution function.
Integer values give vol{u ≥ β} > 1/2 and vol{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2, so β is a median.
A median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| (pointwise comparison on {u ≤ β}, {u > β} and on {u ≥ β}, {u < β}).
|u| ≥ |β| on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let v, G be C¹ with |G| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4. Put a := δ, b := 1 − δ, s := b − a = 1 − 2δ ∈ [1/2, 1], Q := Q_δ = (a, b)ⁿ, Q̄ := [a, b]ⁿ (compact). Write ∂_i v(x) := Dv(x)e_i and G_i := ⟨e_i, G⟩ for the standard orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_n. For i ∈ {1, …, n}, t ∈ ℝ and x' ∈ ℝ^{n−1} let ι_i(t, x') ∈ ℝⁿ be the point whose i-th coordinate is t and whose other coordinates are x' in order (Mathlib Fin.insertNth); put Q' := (a, b)^{n−1} (for n = 1, ℝ⁰ is a point of measure 1).

Facts. (F1) div G(x) = trace DG(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, DG(x)e_i⟩ = Σ_i ∂_iG_i(x) (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner). (F2) Fubini in coordinate i: the map (t, x') ↦ ι_i(t, x') is a measure-preserving bijection ℝ × ℝ^{n−1} → ℝⁿ (Mathlib MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove composed with the measure-preserving identification Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ)) mapping (a, b) × Q' onto Q; hence ∫_Q h = ∫_{Q'} ∫_a^b h(ι_i(t, x')) dt dx' for every h integrable on Q or nonnegative measurable. (F3) v, Dv, G, DG are continuous, hence bounded on Q̄; every function below is a bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure, so all integrals are finite and Fubini applies.

1. Product rule. H := vG is C¹ with DH(x)h = (Dv(x)h) G(x) + v(x) DG(x)h. Hence ∂_i H_i = (∂_i v) G_i + v ∂_i G_i and, by (F1), Σ_i ∂_i H_i(x) = Dv(x)(G(x)) + v(x) div G(x).

2. Divergence theorem on the box. For each i and x' ∈ Q', t ↦ H_i(ι_i(t, x')) is C¹ on [a, b] with derivative ∂_i H_i(ι_i(t, x')), so by the fundamental theorem of calculus ∫_a^b ∂_iH_i(ι_i(t, x')) dt = H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x')). Integrating over x' ∈ Q' and using (F2): ∫_Q ∂_iH_i = ∫_{Q'} [H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x'))] dx'. (This is Mathlib MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable on the box [a, b]^{Fin n}, transported through the measure-preserving identification Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ); that lemma lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem, which must be added as an import to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean if this route is used. The coordinatewise route of steps 2 and 4 needs only intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove and PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, all available under `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`.)

3. Summing over i with step 1: ∫_Q v div G = Σ_i ∫_{Q'}[H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x'))] dx' − ∫_Q Dv(x)(G(x)) dx. Since |H_i| ≤ |v||G| ≤ |v| and |Dv(x)(G(x))| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖|G(x)| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖: |∫_Q v div G| ≤ ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ + Σ_i Σ_{c ∈ {a, b}} ∫_{Q'} |v(ι_i(c, x'))| dx'.

4. Face (trace) estimate. Fix i, c ∈ {a, b} and x' ∈ Q'. For t ∈ [a, b], the fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment between c and t gives |v(ι_i(c, x'))| ≤ |v(ι_i(t, x'))| + ∫_a^b |∂_i v(ι_i(r, x'))| dr. Averaging over t ∈ [a, b] (divide by s > 0): |v(ι_i(c, x'))| ≤ s^{−1} ∫_a^b |v(ι_i(t, x'))| dt + ∫_a^b |∂_i v(ι_i(r, x'))| dr. Integrating over x' ∈ Q' and using (F2): ∫_{Q'} |v(ι_i(c, x'))| dx' ≤ s^{−1} ∫_Q |v| + ∫_Q |∂_i v| ≤ 2 ∫_Q |v| + ∫_Q ‖Dv‖, because s ≥ 1/2 and |∂_i v(x)| = |Dv(x)e_i| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖.

5. Conclusion. There are 2n pairs (i, c), so by steps 3 and 4: |∫_Q v div G| ≤ ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ + 2n(2∫_Q |v| + ∫_Q ‖Dv‖) = (2n + 1) ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ + 4n ∫_Q |v|. With n = m + 1: (2(m + 1) + 1) ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖ + 4(m + 1) ∫_{Q_δ} |v|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Product rule: div(vG) = Dv(G) + v div G, with div = Σ_i ∂_i(·)_i in the standard basis.
Divergence theorem on the box [δ, 1 − δ]ⁿ (FTC in each coordinate plus Fubini): ∫_{Q_δ} ∂_i(vG_i) = face integrals.
|∫ v div G| ≤ ∫‖Dv‖ + Σ over the 2n faces of ∫_face |v|.
Face estimate by FTC and averaging over a side of length s ≥ 1/2: ∫_face |v| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|v| + ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖.
Summing: (2n + 1)∫‖Dv‖ + 4n∫|v|.

subproblems.title: Trace estimate on the unit cube for functions of variation at most V tested on bounded C¹ fields
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure), div g := trace Dg. If w : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} w · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, then for every C¹ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y: |∫_{Q₁} w · div G| ≤ (2n + 1) V + 4n ∫_{Q₁}|w| (2n + 1 = 2(m + 1) + 1, 4n = 4(m + 1)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (w : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), IntegrableOn w {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∀ G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → (∀ y, ‖G y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)| ≤ (2 * (m + 1) + 1) * V + 4 * (m + 1) * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |w y|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (trace estimate; limits σ ↓ 0, then δ ↓ 0), with the mollified functions supplied by the sibling smooth_approx and the smooth estimate by the sibling smooth_trace. In Simon this replaces the appeal to Ch. 2, 2.8–2.9 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 663–676) for the second line of display (32) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1883–1892).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Sibling results used. smooth_approx (cmcdt_cbm_smooth_approx): for w integrable on Q₁ with hyp(w, V) and δ > 0 there are C¹ functions v_k with ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w| → 0. smooth_trace (cmcdt_cbm_smooth_trace): for C¹ v, C¹ G with |G| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4, |∫_{Q_δ} v div G| ≤ (2n + 1)∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v|.

Fix w integrable on Q₁ with hyp(w, V), and G C¹ with |G| ≤ 1.

0. Boundedness of div G. DG is continuous and A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), so div G is continuous; it is therefore bounded on the compact set [0, 1]ⁿ ⊇ Q₁: |div G| ≤ M on Q₁ for some M ≥ 0. Hence w · div G is integrable on Q₁ and on every Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (|w div G| ≤ M|w|).

1. Fix δ ∈ (0, 1/4] and take v_k from smooth_approx (δ > 0). Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ; so v_k, v_k div G and v_k − w are integrable on Q_δ and ε_k := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w| → 0. By smooth_trace (0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4): |∫_{Q_δ} v_k div G| ≤ (2n + 1)∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v_k| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v_k|.

2. Limit k → ∞. |∫_{Q_δ} v_k div G − ∫_{Q_δ} w div G| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w||div G| ≤ M ε_k → 0 and |∫_{Q_δ}|v_k| − ∫_{Q_δ}|w|| ≤ ε_k → 0. Passing to the limit in the inequality of step 1: |∫_{Q_δ} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|w| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w| (Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, |w| ≥ 0).

3. Limit δ ↓ 0. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 4) ∈ (0, 1/4], δ_j ↓ 0; every point of Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. The functions 1_{Q_{δ_j}} w div G converge pointwise on Q₁ to w div G and are dominated by M|w|, which is integrable on Q₁. By dominated convergence, ∫_{Q_{δ_j}} w div G → ∫_{Q₁} w div G. Each term satisfies the bound of step 2, hence so does the limit: |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w| = (2(m + 1) + 1)V + 4(m + 1)∫_{Q₁}|w|. ∎
proof_key_steps: div G is continuous, hence bounded by M on the closed unit cube.
For δ ∈ (0, 1/4]: smooth_approx gives v_k and smooth_trace gives |∫_{Q_δ} v_k div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v_k|.
L¹(Q_δ) convergence and |div G| ≤ M pass this to w: |∫_{Q_δ} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.
Dominated convergence as δ ↓ 0 gives the bound on Q₁.
